errors.english: It is better to have everything come forth [note: perish] and be lifted upon a stake
errors.why: The verse describes having one's entrails all drawn out and being impaled on a stake; the note 'perish' misreads 'byung bar byas pa' (drawn out/extracted).

note: Faithful rendering of the Nāga-king prophecy and the Saṅgha-property verses; only the gloss on one verse misleads.

errors.english: the motion and the fourfold action [note: a specific legal act of the monastic assembly]
errors.why: gsol ba dang bzhi'i las is the jñapticaturtha karman, an act of a motion with three proclamations (the motion being the fourth), not a motion plus a 'fourfold action'.

fix.find: the motion and the fourfold action [note: a specific legal act of the monastic assembly]
fix.replace: an act consisting of a motion followed by three proclamations (jñapticaturtha karman)

errors.english: If those who are in agreement are exhorted through what is not Dharma, there is no downfall. If those who are not in agreement are exhorted through Dharma
errors.why: mthun pa rnams dang / mi mthun pa rnams dang refer to the exhorting assembly being harmonious or not (by a harmonious assembly), not to those who are exhorted.

fix.find: If those who are in agreement are exhorted through what is not Dharma, there is no downfall. If those who are not in agreement are exhorted through Dharma
fix.replace: If one is exhorted by a harmonious assembly through what is not Dharma, there is no downfall. If one is exhorted by a non-harmonious assembly through Dharma

note: Commentary on the tenth saṃghāvaśeṣa is broadly followed, but the formal-act term and the no-offence clauses (who is harmonious) are wrong.
Accurate rendering of the fire-example argument and the root verses on seeing, with the gone/not-gone parallel correctly worked out.

errors.english: then one might wonder if it is contradictory with the result of lightness or contradictory with the (pervader)
errors.why: The anticipated doubt is that lightness is contradictory with the effect (heaviness) or with the pervader, not that sin is contradictory with a 'result of lightness'.

fix.find: then one might wonder if it is contradictory with the result of lightness or contradictory with the (pervader)
fix.replace: then one might suspect that lightness is contradictory with the effect or contradictory with the (pervader)

errors.english: Furthermore, heaviness is not the result of sin, because perception and (non-perception) the logical proof of absence; original: mi dmigs pa are absent.
errors.why: The Tibetan marks this as an anticipated doubt (zhes dogs pa'o); the English presents it as the author's own assertion.

errors.english: its (samskara) mental formations or conditioning; original: 'du byེད་ is not heavy
errors.why: Here 'du byed is the karmic impression/trace left by sin, not the skandha of mental formations.

note: Follows the commentary on consecration and sin in outline, but misplaces who is contradictory with what and turns a doubt into an assertion.
The objection-and-refutation sequence on attainment, doubt and familiarity is rendered accurately with speakers correctly assigned.

errors.english: future things are not understood in the same way that form is seen to exist subsequently through the perception of taste as an effect
errors.why: The example is itself not understood: just as from perceiving taste one does not understand that form will exist later too; the English implies the later form is understood.

errors.english: Understanding the existence of the cause of a taste is included within the understanding of a potentiality that is capable of producing a form without obstruction.
errors.why: The sentence (begun on the previous side) says the understanding of form is included in understanding that the cause of taste has unobstructed capacity to produce form; the English changes what is included in what.

note: Sound rendering of the inference-from-cause discussion with two passages whose logical relation is slightly garbled.

errors.english: on the path of meditation [note: Sanskrit: (bhāvanāmārga)], which pertains to the three vehicles, the subtle and very subtle defilements
errors.why: rjes gnas pa'i qualifies the stains (the subtle stains that remain in the three vehicles), not the path of meditation.

errors.english: Through the forbearance of the doctrine regarding the path
errors.why: chos shes bzod pa is dharmajñānakṣānti, forbearance toward the knowledge of dharma, not 'forbearance of the doctrine'.

note: Verse on the path of seeing rendered as prose but the content (abandonments, 88 afflictions, bodhyaṅgas, first bhūmi) is accurate.

errors.english: engaging with meaningless things like material entities
errors.why: dngos po here is 'entity/existent' (bhāva) as a concept and don med pa means objectless/nonexistent, not 'meaningless material entities'; 'material entities' recurs through the page.

note: Accurate rendering of the rebirth argument from homogeneous seeds, apart from the recurrent 'material entities' for dngos po.

errors.english: Thus, the elder brother, acting as a devoted friend [note: Sanskrit: iti snigdhasya suhridah], gathered his courage.
errors.why: dang por skyes pa (agrajanman) is 'the brahmin', who gave firmness/encouragement to his affectionate friend; there is no elder brother and he does not gather his own courage.

fix.find: Thus, the elder brother, acting as a devoted friend [note: Sanskrit: iti snigdhasya suhridah], gathered his courage.
fix.replace: Thus the brahmin, having encouraged his affectionate friend [note: Sanskrit: iti snigdhasya suhridah],

errors.english: the Brahmin elder [note: referring to the elder brother of Kapila]
errors.why: The Tibetan names the brahmin Kapila (Sanskrit kapilasya agrajanmanaḥ, 'of the brahmin Kapila'); the note invents an elder brother of Kapila.

errors.english: the lineage of Nyagrodha-Kapila, born from the Kashyapa clan
errors.why: Nyagrodha is a simile (the Kāśyapa-born family is like a banyan in the world), not part of a personal name.

note: Narrative of the golden image and Bhadrā is followable, but the brahmin go-between is turned into an 'elder brother' and a simile into a name.

errors.english: [note: Tibetan: ma bsdoms, meaning "unrestrained" or "undisciplined" in a literal sense, but here used as a proper name]
errors.why: ma bsdams renders the name Anaṅgaṇa ('unblemished/unbound'); glossing it as 'undisciplined' misleads about the name's sense.

note: Faithful rendering of the Vipaśyin/Anaṅgaṇa story and the rival offerings of householder and king.
